explanations: luna: The source explains الدِّين as repayment and recompense; “يوم الدين” names the day on which that settlement belongs to God. | terra: مَٰلِكِ يَوْمِ ٱلدِّينِ names God as sovereign of the day when recompense is due, the title under which the section's account closes.

luna: The source's accepted counterfeit is a failed valuation; here those who buy misguidance find “فما ربحت تجارتهم,” a trade with no profit. | terra: Buying error for guidance yields a trade with no profit, a moral misvaluation expressed in market terms.
terra: The command not to exchange God's signs for a small price identifies revelation as something market valuation must not cheapen.
terra: No soul can settle for another on the judgment day and no equivalent ransom is accepted, setting a firm boundary on debt transfer and payment.
terra: أَتَسْتَبْدِلُونَ ٱلَّذِى هُوَ أَدْنَىٰ بِٱلَّذِى هُوَ خَيْرٌ rebukes exchanging the lower for the better, the section's valuation error stated as a failed trade.
terra: Those who manufacture scripture for a small price receive woe both for what their hands wrote and for what they earned, turning fraudulent production into a debit.
terra: Those who purchase worldly life with the Hereafter receive unabated punishment, a disastrous exchange between passing and lasting value.
terra: The ayah calls the price for which they sold themselves evil: rejection born of envy turns the self into badly valued merchandise.

terra: Those who purchase magic know that its buyer has no خَلَاقٍ in the Hereafter, and the ayah condemns the price for which they sold themselves; measured share and ruinous valuation meet explicitly.

luna: This describes people selling revelation for a small price and losing the promised divine address and purification, a failed bargain that parallels the source's worthless coin. | terra: Those who conceal revelation purchase only a small price and consume fire, so apparent market gain is reassessed as punishment.
terra: Buying error for guidance and punishment for forgiveness treats final liabilities as a ruinous exchange.
terra: One petitioner asks only for this world and has no خَلَاقٍ in the Hereafter, showing an allotted share lost through narrow valuation.

luna: The source describes each person's measured share; here people receive a share of what they earned and God is swift in account. | terra: These petitioners have a نَصِيبٌ مِّمَّا كَسَبُوا and God is swift in account, directly joining an allotted share to what was earned.
terra: One person sells himself seeking God's pleasure, a positive self-exchange whose value is fixed by its divine object.
terra: Worldly life is made attractive to disbelievers, while God provides the God-fearing without account on resurrection, correcting apparent present value.
terra: Apostasy through death makes works void in both worlds, a direct case of accumulated labor losing all final assay value.
luna: The source's dictionary gloss links work and wage; this gives a concrete case, requiring payment of wages to women who nurse the child.

luna: The source's debt gloss includes giving; this calls for a “قرضا حسنا” to God and promises its multiplication, making lending and return concrete. | terra: A good loan to God is multiplied many times and all are returned to Him, translating lending into eschatological return.
terra: Believers must spend before a day on which no trade, friendship, or intercession operates, marking the end of ordinary market remedies.
terra: Those who spend without following their gift by مَنّ or injury retain their wage; the other Quranic sense of م ن ن shows how a payment can be spoiled by being held over its recipient.
terra: Charity is invalidated by مَنّ and injury like soil stripped from a smooth rock, a vivid case of apparent value failing when assayed.
terra: Believers must not select defective goods for giving when they themselves would accept them only with eyes closed; payment must carry value the payer recognizes.

luna: The source's labor-and-wage image has a parallel in spending: what is spent is repaid in full and the giver is not wronged. | terra: Whatever good is spent is repaid in full and the spender is not wronged, a charitable instance of exact settlement.
terra: Creditors retain only their principal, neither wronging nor being wronged, defining a just boundary for repayment.
terra: A debtor in hardship receives deferment, and remission is better; the literal debt relation introduces mercy into exact accounting.

luna: On return to God every soul is paid in full for what it earned and is not wronged, a concise counterpart to the source's closed account. | terra: A day of return to God ends with every soul paid in full for what it earned and no injustice, a concise version of the section's entire account.

luna: The source glosses د ي ن as debt-dealing in giving or taking; this ayah uses “تداينتم بدين” for a debt due at a term and orders it recorded. | terra: إِذَا تَدَايَنتُم بِدَيْنٍ stages the named د ي ن sense literally: a deferred debt is measured, written, witnessed, and protected from diminution.
terra: God is قَائِمًا بِٱلْقِسْطِ and declares His unique divinity with the witnesses, joining the ق و م field to the maintenance of exact justice.
terra: Denial and murderous opposition leave deeds void in this world and the Hereafter, so no final value remains.

luna: At the gathering, each soul is paid in full for what it earned and none is wronged; the verse makes the source's equitable wage concrete. | terra: On the undoubted gathering day every soul is paid in full for what it earned and none is wronged.
terra: God gives provision without account to whom He wills, a non-wage formulation of quantity unbounded by ordinary reckoning.
terra: Mary receives provision from God without account, making unmeasured giving concrete within a sanctuary scene.

luna: Believers who do good are paid their wages in full here, making explicit the source's claim that righteous work receives its due. | terra: Those who believe and do righteous works are paid their wages in full, and the denial of love for wrongdoers guards the judgment's justice.
terra: A qintar and a single دينار test two trustees; one returns the deposit and one withholds it unless pressed, bringing coin, exact value, and repayment into one moral assay.

luna: The source's coin tests what something is worth; this ayah condemns people who sell God's covenant and oaths for a small price, trading away their share in the Hereafter. | terra: Those who exchange God's covenant for a small price receive no خَلَاقَ in the Hereafter, uniting false pricing with the section's measured-share sense of the word.
terra: Even an earthful of gold cannot be accepted as ransom from one who dies rejecting faith, setting a boundary on coin's power at the final account.
terra: People do not reach full righteousness until they spend from what they love, making surrendered value part of the assay.
terra: Forgiveness and enduring gardens are called the excellent wage of workers, another explicit worker-to-wage formulation.
terra: Betrayed property must be brought on resurrection, after which every soul is paid in full for what it earned and none is wronged; fraudulent taking and exact settlement share one ayah.

luna: The believers rejoice that God does not waste the believers' reward, a specific parallel to payment that is not withheld. | terra: The faithful rejoice that God does not waste the believers' wage, stating preservation of earned value.
terra: Those who purchase disbelief with faith cannot harm God and receive painful punishment, another exchange that reveals its true price only at judgment.
terra: Death precedes the day when people are paid أُجُورَكُمْ in full; the ayah then devalues worldly life as deceptive merchandise.

luna: Those who cast the covenant behind their backs and sell it for a small price enact the source's image of misvaluing what is entrusted to them. | terra: People throw the scripture behind them and purchase a small price, which the ayah judges an evil acquisition.
terra: God says He does not let the work of any worker be lost, making the worker's identity and labor answerable to an unfailing payer.
terra: Believers from the People of the Book do not exchange God's signs for a small price and therefore retain their wage with their Lord.
terra: Property is something God made قِيَامًا for people, preserving the ق و م sense of that by which life stands rather than merely its assessed price.
luna: The source's share gloss is concretely echoed by the allotted share of inheritance given to men and women.
luna: The inheritance portions here are fixed by stated ratios, a legal instance of the source's measured share assigned to each person.
luna: This continues the inheritance allotments with explicit fractions for spouses and siblings, extending the measured shares in the preceding ayah.

luna: The source's dictionary form الخلاق means a measured share; this verse says men and women each have a share of what they earn. | terra: Men and women each have a نَصِيبٌ from what they earned, a clear Quranic form of the allotted share attached to work.
luna: This assigns heirs their portion of what parents and relatives leave, a direct instance of the source's measured-share sense.

luna: God does not wrong even an atom's weight, doubles good, and grants a great wage; the smallest measure here safeguards the source's complete payment. | terra: God does not wrong even an atom's weight, multiplies a good deed, and grants a great wage, combining minute assay and generous payment.
terra: Those given a share of scripture purchase error and wish others to lose the way, spending received value on loss.
terra: People who certify their own purity are corrected: God appraises whom He wills and wrongs no one even by a tiny thread.
terra: God commands trusts to be returned and judgment between people to be made with justice, directly enacting the section's definition of حكم as a just decision.
terra: The call to fight addresses those who sell the worldly life for the Hereafter and promises a great wage whether slain or victorious.
terra: Worldly enjoyment is called little, the Hereafter better for the God-fearing, and no one is wronged even by a thread on a date stone.

luna: The source pairs believers' good work with a lasting wage; this ayah likewise joins faith and righteous action to reward, adding “لا يظلمون نقيرا.” | terra: The section explicitly invokes this ayah: faithful righteous work is admitted to the Garden and is not underpaid even by a نَقِيرًا, the tiniest pit in a date stone.
terra: The command to be قَوَّامِينَ بِٱلْقِسْطِ requires testimony against self or kin and refuses to let wealth or poverty distort the appraisal.

luna: Hypocrites are assigned the lowest depth of the Fire; this gives “the lowest” in the source's fall image a concrete eschatological counterpart. | terra: Hypocrites are assigned to the lowest depth of the Fire, turning the section's س ف ل baseness into an exact eschatological rank.
terra: Faithful righteous workers are paid their wages fully and receive additional bounty, showing that exact payment need not exclude grace.
luna: The final inheritance ruling assigns siblings specified portions, another concrete instance of shares measured for each.
terra: Whoever rejects faith has his work voided and becomes one of the losers in the Hereafter, the result of failed moral assay.
terra: Believers must stand firmly as just witnesses and not let hatred cause an inequitable judgment, bringing ق و م into the practice of the section's just measure.
terra: The covenant asks for a good loan to God and promises expiation and gardens, a debt idiom whose return exceeds the advance.
terra: All the earth and as much again cannot ransom disbelief from punishment, so worldly holdings cannot discharge this debt.
terra: If judgment is undertaken it must be بالقسط, and God loves those who act equitably, explaining what the supreme Judge's حكم looks like in human practice.
terra: The command not to exchange God's signs for a small price makes faithful judgment the alternative to corrupt valuation.

luna: The source glosses ح ك م as judgment by justice; this asks “ومن أحسن من الله حكما,” directly echoing the question of the best judge. | terra: وَمَنْ أَحْسَنُ مِنَ ٱللَّهِ حُكْمًا is a rhetorical counterpart to أَحْكَمِ ٱلْحَاكِمِينَ and opposes God's judgment to the judgment of ignorance.
terra: Witnesses must not exchange their oath for a price even when kin could benefit, preserving truthful valuation in an estate account.

luna: God alone has judgment and is the best of decision-makers; this parallels the source's final claim that judgment belongs to the just judge. | terra: إِنِ ٱلْحُكْمُ إِلَّا لِلَّهِ reserves judgment to God, whose true decision separates the parties.

luna: This combines return, “الحكم,” and the swiftest accounting; the source likewise closes its image with return before the just judge and final reckoning. | terra: The section explicitly links this return to the whole accounting image: creatures are returned to their true Master, الحكم belongs to Him, and He is swiftest in حساب.

luna: A soul faces what it earned and cannot have its ransom accepted; this sets a limit beside the source's image of dues and final settlement. | terra: Every soul is held for what it earned, and no ransom or equivalent payment is accepted apart from God, combining liability, earnings, and the impossibility of buying off the account.
terra: Even the named prophets' works would be void if they associated partners, stating the boundary under which work retains value.

luna: The command “وأوفوا الكيل والميزان بالقسط” gives a just-measure counterpart to the source's full-weight coin. | terra: The command to fulfill measure and weight بالقسط, followed by the rule that no soul bears beyond capacity, binds exact commerce to exact moral charge.

luna: The return is measured here: a good deed earns tenfold while evil earns only its like, and no one is wronged. | terra: A good deed receives tenfold while an evil one receives only its like, and neither side is wronged; final payment is exact yet gracious.
terra: Each soul earns only against itself, bears no other's burden, and returns to the Lord for disclosure, joining personal earnings to final return.

luna: The source's calibrated coin meets the explicit image of the balance of judgment: “الوزن يومئذ الحق” makes truthful weighing the standard. | terra: ٱلْوَزْنُ يَوْمَئِذٍ ٱلْحَقُّ makes the resurrection's weighing true, and heavy scales identify those whose value endures.

luna: The underweight side of the source's coin image is realized by people whose scales are light and who lose themselves; the verse states the adverse result. | terra: Light scales expose people who have made themselves lose, an explicit counterpart to the coin that fails assay and falls among the worthless.

luna: The people of Midian are told to give full measure and weight and not diminish people's goods; this is the same fair-assessment standard as the coin image. | terra: Shuayb commands full measure and weight and forbids diminishing people's goods, a literal market version of undiminished payment.
terra: Shuayb asks God to judge between the two groups in truth and calls Him the best of judges, locating fair judgment within the same prophet's market dispute.
terra: Pharaoh's magicians ask whether there will be an أجر if they prevail, showing wage as a promised return for performance, though from a corrupt payer.
terra: Denying God's signs and the meeting of the Hereafter voids works, and the question says they receive only the recompense of what they did.
terra: Those who hold to the Book and establish prayer are assured that God does not waste the wage of reformers.
luna: People who fail to use their hearts, eyes, and ears are likened to cattle or worse, a specific moral descent from the source's best-formed human.
luna: The fixed one-fifth allocation of the spoils is a concrete instance of the source's dictionary gloss that a share is measured out for each.
terra: Whatever is spent in God's way is repaid in full without injustice, another concrete outlay-and-return account.
terra: Selling God's signs for a small price leads people to block His way, exposing the moral cost hidden by the quoted price.
terra: The self-claimed service of shrine-tending cannot survive open disbelief; its workers' deeds are declared void.
terra: Hoarded gold and silver that are not spent become grounds for painful punishment, reversing stored monetary value.
terra: The treasured metal is heated and used to brand its owners, turning the coin-like asset itself into evidence in the account.
terra: Satisfaction with the nearer life is rebuked because its enjoyment is only little beside the Hereafter.
terra: God makes the disbelievers' word السُّفْلَىٰ and His word highest, a direct high-low judgment of worth.
terra: People consume their خَلَاق as earlier peoples consumed theirs and end with void works, showing an allotted worldly share spent without retaining final value.

luna: The market image becomes an explicit divine transaction: God “اشترى” believers' lives and property for Paradise, so the reader sees faith and effort as a sale with a promised return. | terra: God purchases believers' lives and wealth for the Garden and calls it the greatest triumph, a divine exchange that assigns their highest price.

luna: After describing the believers' costly mobilization, this says God does not waste the wage of the good-doers; 9:121 records even small expenses and journeys. | terra: Recorded thirst, fatigue, and effort are justified by the rule that God does not waste the wage of good-doers.

luna: This specifies what the previous verse's wage covers: every small or large expense and valley crossed is recorded before reward is paid. | terra: Every expenditure and journey is written so that God may recompense the best of the workers' deeds, joining ledger entry and wage.

luna: Wrongdoers would offer all the earth as ransom, but judgment is made justly; this gives the source's payment-and-verdict image its boundary for those who owe an account. | terra: A wrongdoer would offer everything on earth as ransom, but judgment is made بالقسط and no one is wronged, showing that the final account cannot be bought off.
terra: No action and no atom's weight escapes the clear record, giving the final appraisal exhaustive precision.
terra: The command is to wait until God judges, followed by وَهُوَ خَيْرُ ٱلْحَٰكِمِينَ, a close verbal counterpart to surah 95's final question.
luna: This joins patience and righteous work to forgiveness and a great wage, another concrete formulation of the source's labor receiving its due.
terra: Those who want only worldly display are paid their works in full here and suffer no shortfall here, a deliberately limited settlement.
terra: The same works prove void in the Hereafter and yield only Fire, showing that a payment received in one market may carry no final value.
terra: Noah addresses God as أَحْكَمُ ٱلْحَٰكِمِينَ while asking about a painful family case, placing supreme judgment above a human claim.

luna: The command to give full measure and weight in just balance directly parallels the source's coin assessed at its proper weight. | terra: Shuayb forbids reducing measure and weight while warning of an encompassing day, connecting crooked valuation with judgment.

luna: This continuation forbids diminishing people's due, the commercial fraud opposite to the source's exact calibration. | terra: Full measure, just weight, and the ban on depriving people of their things define the honest assay against which the section's coin is tested.
terra: بَقِيَّتُ ٱللَّهِ خَيْرٌ contrasts the gain God leaves with profit made by false measure, a direct valuation of what truly remains.
terra: The blessed remain in the Garden through an عَطَاءً غَيْرَ مَجْذُوذٍ, an uncut gift that states without م م ن wording what the section hears in غَيْرُ مَمْنُونٍ.
terra: Each person is fully repaid for deeds, and God's complete knowledge secures the accuracy of the settlement.
terra: Patience is commanded because God does not waste the wage of good-doers, a preservation counterpart to the uncurtailed payment.

luna: The source's coin scene names dirhams and tests their worth; Joseph is sold for counted dirhams at a low price, making the undervaluing of a human explicit. | terra: Yusuf is sold for a paltry price in counted dirhams because the sellers assign him little value, a human undervaluation of a finely made person.
terra: إِنِ ٱلْحُكْمُ إِلَّا لِلَّهِ reserves judgment to God and then calls exclusive worship ٱلدِّينُ ٱلْقَيِّمُ, bringing حكم, د ي ن, and ق و م together in their rule-and-uprightness senses.
terra: Yusuf's earthly establishment illustrates that God does not waste the wage of good-doers, though the payment here begins before the final account.
terra: Yusuf describes himself as one who gives full measure, making honest provision the opposite of curtailed payment.
terra: The brothers find their merchandise returned and anticipate obtaining measure again, bringing ر د د into a concrete exchange-and-provision setting.
terra: Jacob is entrusted to decide until God judges, and God is called the best of judges, distinguishing patient human waiting from final decision.
terra: In hardship the brothers ask Yusuf to fulfill the measure and treat the excess as charity, distinguishing an exact commercial due from a gift.
terra: Joseph links reverence and patience to the principle that God does not waste the wage of good-doers.
luna: The source's dictionary gloss says each person's share is measured; this states that everything has a measure with God.
terra: Those who refuse their Lord would offer the earth twice over as ransom, yet theirs is the evil account; no proposed payment can revise the appraisal.

luna: God expands provision for some and restricts it for others; this makes the source's measured allocation concrete and contrasts it with people judging worldly abundance as ultimate value. | terra: Expanded or restricted provision does not alter that worldly life is only a small enjoyment beside the Hereafter.

luna: The deeds of disbelievers are compared to ash scattered by wind, leaving them with no power over what they earned; this is a specific image of value dissipating at assessment. | terra: Disbelieving works become ashes scattered by a violent wind, leaving their owners unable to retain any of what they earned.
terra: Spending must occur before the day with neither bargaining nor friendship, so present wealth cannot be offered after the account opens.

luna: Provision is sent down only in known measure, a specific parallel to the source's measured allocation of each person's share. | terra: Created stores are sent down only in a known measure, a cosmic version of provision being allotted rather than random.

luna: God creates people, then some are returned to the feeblest age and forget what they knew; this is a direct decline from the source's well-formed human. | terra: God creates, causes death, and يردّ some people to the most abject age; the same ر د د movement turns human fitness back toward incapacity.

luna: The source's market tests what a thing is worth; this forbids exchanging God's covenant for a small price and says what is with God is better. | terra: The covenant must not be exchanged for a small price because what is with God is better, a direct refusal of undervaluation.

luna: Those who endure are paid according to the best of what they did; it specifies the source's work-and-wage link and contrasts passing gain with what is with God. | terra: What people possess runs out while what is with God remains, and the patient are paid their wage by the best of their works; permanence and payment meet explicitly.

luna: The promise of good life and wages for believers' best work develops the source's reward for righteous labor. | terra: Believing workers of righteousness receive a good life and a wage based on the best they did, matching the section's work-for-wage account.

luna: This day each soul receives the full result of its work without injustice, matching the source's promise of an unshortened settlement. | terra: Every soul comes pleading for itself, is fully paid what it did, and is not wronged: the worker meets the account personally.
terra: Each person's record is fastened to him and will be brought out as an open book, giving the account an individual ledger.
terra: The command to read one's own book makes the person sufficient as reckoner against himself.

luna: The source describes a coin that is neither short nor excessive; this commands full measure and weighing with the straight balance. | terra: The ayah commands full measure and weighing with the straight balance, then calls that better in final outcome.

luna: God's honoring of Adam's children establishes their high worth, a useful boundary against the source's later fall to the lowest state. | terra: God honors the children of Adam, provides them good things, and favors them over much creation, a divine valuation of the human being.

luna: At the gathering people are called with their records and are not wronged even by a thread's weight, joining the source's account with exact measure. | terra: Those given their record in the right hand read it and are not wronged even by a tiny thread, combining the ledger with minute exactness.
terra: The upright book is قَيِّمًا and immediately promises faithful righteous workers a good wage, placing moral straightness and recompense in one ayah.
terra: The companions send a silver coin to purchase food and seek what is purest; it is a literal coin scene, though it does not itself stage final appraisal.

luna: The source glosses أَجْرٌ as the wage for work; this promise says God will not waste the wage of anyone who does good work. | terra: God does not waste the wage of anyone who does good work, a direct statement that sound workmanship retains its value.
terra: Wealth and children are temporary adornment, while enduring good deeds are better with the Lord in reward and hope, an explicit divine appraisal.

luna: The opened record omits neither small nor large deeds and God wrongs no one; it shows how the source's final account leaves no value unexamined. | terra: The record omits neither small nor great, deeds are found present, and the Lord wrongs no one, an exhaustive audit.
terra: Moses notes that a wage could have been taken for repairing the wall, another literal job-price that clarifies أجر.
terra: The question identifies the greatest losers by their works, inviting appraisal of labor that its workers mistakenly count as valuable.

luna: This ayah says the losers thought they were doing well while their effort was lost; 18:105 supplies the source-related verdict that their deeds receive no weight. | terra: Their effort is lost in worldly life while they think they are doing fine work, the self-deception of a failed assay.

luna: The preceding 18:104 says these people thought they were doing well; this ayah says their deeds are null and receive no “وزنا” on Judgment Day. | terra: Those whose works collapse through denial receive no وَزْنًا on resurrection; نُقِيمُ also brings the section's ق و م field into a judgment where failed deeds have no assay value.
terra: After 18:105 removes all weight from their deeds, this ayah names their recompense as Hell for denial and mockery.
terra: Enduring righteous deeds are declared better with the Lord in reward and return, measuring lasting work against transient holdings.
terra: Faithful righteous action need fear neither injustice nor diminution, making non-reduction the result of the final assay.
terra: The flower of worldly life is only a test, while the Lord's provision is better and more lasting.

luna: The source's full-weight coin evokes an exact balance; here the scales are set for judgment, and not even a mustard-seed weight is omitted or unjustly treated. | terra: Just scales are set for resurrection, no soul is wronged, and even a mustard seed is brought to account: the section's assay becomes an explicitly eschatological weighing.
terra: The plea رَبِّ ٱحْكُم بِٱلْحَقِّ asks the Lord to judge in truth, the proper stance before the section's final Judge.

luna: The source moves from the human in best measure to the lowest state; this creation sequence ends with some returned to the most decrepit age, a bodily reversal. | terra: In an argument for resurrection, some humans are يُرَدُّ إِلَىٰ أَرْذَلِ ٱلْعُمُرِ until knowledge is lost, closely paralleling the section's reversal from fine making to low condition.

luna: The stages of human formation culminate in a new creation and the praise “أحسن الخالقين,” a close parallel to the source's excellent human form. | terra: The staged human creation culminates in another creation and praise of the best of creators, a Quranic appraisal of formed humanity.
terra: The question asks whether wealth and children are being advanced as proof of good value, exposing a mistaken reading of worldly provision.
terra: The answer says they do not perceive the truth, refusing wealth and offspring as a reliable divine appraisal.
terra: A record speaks truth and no one is wronged, while no soul is charged beyond capacity; assessment and evidence match.

luna: Like the source's measured coin, deeds are literally weighed here; the heavy scales mark success. | terra: Heavy scales at judgment mark the successful, repeating the section's full-weight standard in eschatological form.

luna: This is the reverse outcome to the source's full-weight coin: light scales mean loss and abiding punishment. | terra: Light scales mean self-loss and lasting punishment, the moral analogue of failing the money changer's test.
terra: God will يُوَفِّيهِمُ ٱللَّهُ دِينَهُمُ ٱلْحَقَّ: دِين is their true due and God pays it in full, almost a compact statement of the section's payment reading.
luna: Trade and sale are named directly, then set against fear of the day of account; this joins the source's marketplace and final reckoning.

luna: The people occupied with trade in 24:37 receive this ayah's payoff: God rewards their best deeds and increases them from His bounty. | terra: God recompenses workers by the best they did, adds from His bounty, and provides without account, joining appraised work to payment beyond a curtailed measure.

luna: The connection is analogical: the source's apparently accepted coin is exposed as false when assessed, while this scene's apparent water proves to be a mirage when reached; both reverse an expected value. | terra: Disbelieving deeds are a mirage that looks like water until nothing is found; instead the person finds God, who pays his account in full.

luna: The source's خ ل ق dictionary branch describes a share measured for each; this says God created everything and determined it with precise determination. | terra: God creates everything and determines it with exact determination, grounding measured value in the Creator's act rather than the market alone.

luna: The source's counterfeit becomes valueless when tested; here deeds people thought valuable are made “هباء منثورا,” a specific reversal of their assumed worth. | terra: Works that appeared substantial are made scattered dust, a direct image of value rejected at divine inspection.
luna: The same comparison says many people are like cattle or further astray, another direct reversal of the source's elevated human measure.
luna: The source uses ق و م for pricing and exact adjustment; this verse uses قواما for balanced spending, a related but different sense of measured proportion.
terra: The magicians again seek a wage for victory, a literal payment bargain that contrasts with divine recompense.
terra: Abraham hopes for forgiveness on يَوْمِ ٱلدِّينِ, showing that the day of payment also admits mercy.
terra: The day when neither wealth nor children benefit rejects the two common human measures of worth.

luna: This opens the same practical measuring scene as the source's accurately adjusted coin, requiring full measure. | terra: Fulfilling the measure and refusing to make others losers states the payment ethic in literal commercial terms.
luna: The next command specifies the source's full-weight image: weigh with the straight balance. | terra: The straight balance is the section's full-standard coin tested by an honest scale.

luna: This ayah forbids reducing people's due after the measuring commands, naming the fraud opposite to the source's exact calibration. | terra: The prohibition on diminishing people's goods identifies social corruption as a falsified valuation.
terra: The measuring commands culminate in fear of the One who خَلَقَكُمْ, joining just commercial measure to the Creator who measured human beings.
terra: The Lord decides the disputes of the Children of Israel by His حكم, specifying the knowledgeable and powerful Judge behind the decision.
terra: The invitation is expressly to pay Moses أَجْرَ مَا سَقَيْتَ لَنَا, a literal wage for completed work that anchors the section's أجر as work's return.

luna: The source names أَجْرٌ as work's wage; here a worker is assessed as strong and trustworthy before being hired, linking human valuation to paid work. | terra: The proposal to hire Moses values strength and trustworthiness as the qualities of a good paid worker.

luna: The employment agreement uses the source's أجر root for serving a stated term; it makes the work-for-return relation concrete. | terra: The father offers marriage in return for eight years of Moses' service and leaves two more voluntary, specifying a negotiated term of labor after 28:26's hiring proposal.
terra: Worldly goods are temporary enjoyment and adornment, while what is with God is better and lasting, a direct comparison of appraised value.
terra: A person promised the good promise and meeting it is contrasted with one briefly provisioned then brought for judgment.
terra: People dazzled by Qarun call his display a mighty fortune, voicing a worldly market appraisal.
terra: Those given knowledge answer that God's reward is better for faithful good workers and is received by the patient, correcting 28:79's valuation.
luna: Believers who do good are promised recompense for their best deeds, directly extending the source's work-and-wage relation.
terra: The promised dwellings for faithful good workers end with نِعْمَ أَجْرُ ٱلْعَامِلِينَ, explicitly joining أجر and عاملين.

terra: The command to set one's face to the dīn invokes the fitrah upon which God خَلَقَ people and calls it ٱلدِّينُ ٱلْقَيِّمُ, joining creation, proportionate fit, and the semantic range of دِين and ق و م.

luna: Human life passes from weakness to strength and back to weakness and gray hair, a specific reversal of the source's high-to-low human trajectory. | terra: Creation moves from weakness to strength and back to weakness and grayness, another arc in which human condition loses its initial force.
terra: Purchasing distracting speech to mislead others turns expenditure into a humiliating liability.
terra: A mustard seed hidden in rock, heaven, or earth is brought forth by God, so even concealed moral weight enters the account.

luna: The source's image of a human made in best measure parallels “أحسن كل شيء خلقه” and the beginning of human creation here. | terra: God makes good everything He created and begins human creation from clay, another Quranic statement of sound created workmanship.
terra: Those sparing with support and abusive after fear passes have their works nullified by God, so outward participation proves debased.
terra: Not an atom's weight, smaller, or greater escapes God; all is in a clear record used to answer the denial of resurrection.
terra: God gathers the parties and judges between them in truth, uniting final assembly with the decisive valuation.
terra: Wealth and children do not bring people near; faith and righteous work receive multiplied recompense, correcting the market's status scale.

luna: The source begins with the marketplace and pricing; this ayah calls faithful worship and giving a “تجارة لن تبور,” a trade that does not fail. | terra: Recitation, prayer, and spending are called a trade that will never perish, preparing for the full wage in 35:30.

luna: The trade in 35:29 is completed by this ayah's promise to pay the traders' wages in full and increase them; the verse contributes the settlement. | terra: God pays the reciters and spenders their wages in full and adds from His bounty, a settlement greater than strict equivalence.

luna: The source links deeds to wages; this says no soul is wronged and people are repaid only for what they did. | terra: The judgment permits no injustice and recompenses people only for what they did, stating exact equivalence between work and return.

luna: Long life can invert a person's creation here; “ننكسه في الخلق” makes a reversal of the source's best-form image explicit. | terra: Whomever God grants long life He reverses in creation, a nonlexical parallel to the image of a well-formed human losing the condition in which he was first assayed.
terra: At resurrection the deniers recognize هَٰذَا يَوْمُ ٱلدِّينِ, the day whose liability they had questioned in 37:53.

luna: The source identifies “لمدينون” as asking whether they will receive their due; this speaker's incredulous question voices that same resistance to recompense. | terra: The resurrected skeptic asks whether death and dust will leave him لَمَدِينُونَ, directly voicing disbelief that a final recompense will be exacted.
terra: The plotters against Abraham are made ٱلْأَسْفَلِينَ, turning their intended mastery into divinely assigned lowness.
terra: The mockers demand that their قِطَّنَا, their allotted portion, be hastened before the Day of Account, turning a measured share into sarcasm about final payment.

luna: David is commanded to judge between people with truth, and warned about forgetting the Day of Account; this brings just judgment and reckoning together. | terra: David is commanded to judge people in truth and not follow desire, a human office measured against the just divine حكم.
terra: The declaration that God's provision has no exhaustion directly parallels a reward whose amount is neither cut down nor used up.

luna: The source quotes this exact promise: those who endure receive their wages “بغير حساب,” a payment not cut down by reckoning. | terra: The section explicitly hears غَيْرُ مَمْنُونٍ as an unmeasured, undiminished wage; this ayah says the patient are paid أَجْرَهُم بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍ, making that reading concrete.
terra: God removes the worst of faithful workers' deeds and pays their wage according to the best, identifying the standard used in valuation.
terra: Wrongdoers would ransom themselves with everything on earth doubled, but the judgment discloses a liability wealth could not price.
terra: Association would nullify even the addressee's work and place him among the losers, an explicit warning that the coin of labor can fail completely.

luna: The people are judged with truth here; the following ayah pays each soul for its deeds, giving the source's just account a parallel scene. | terra: At the final gathering the record and witnesses are brought and judgment is rendered بالحق without injustice, staging the section's just closing of the books.

luna: The source's العمل / أجر connection meets this statement that every soul is paid for what it did; the judge knows their deeds. | terra: Following 39:69's judgment, every soul is paid in full for what it did, the exact settlement after valuation.
terra: The inheritors of the Garden call it نِعْمَ أَجْرُ ٱلْعَامِلِينَ, recognizing the final allotment as the workers' excellent wage.
terra: The answer to rejected exclusive worship is that الحكم belongs to God, the Exalted and Great, reserving final decision to Him.

luna: Every soul is paid for what it earned, with no injustice and swift accounting; this closely matches the source's final fair settlement. | terra: Each soul is recompensed for what it earned, with no injustice and a swift حساب, directly joining wages to the final ledger.
luna: God judges in truth while those invoked besides Him cannot judge; this makes the source's claim of God's uniquely sound judgment concrete.
terra: The believing speaker calls this worldly life temporary enjoyment and the Hereafter the lasting home.
terra: A believer who works righteousness enters the Garden and is provided there without account, a close parallel to the section's unmeasured wage.

luna: This repeated formulation says God shaped people and made their forms beautiful, a direct parallel to the source's valuation of human form. | terra: God forms humans and makes their forms good, then provides good things and identifies Himself as their Lord, joining good formation to provision and return.
luna: This describes the human's creation from dust and stages of life, then notes that some are returned to decrepit age, joining the source's fit form to its decline.

luna: This repeats the source's combination of faith, good work, and an “أجر غير ممنون,” directly clarifying its unshortened wage. | terra: Faith and righteous work receive أَجْرٌ غَيْرُ مَمْنُونٍ, the exact reward formula whose measured yet uncurtailed force the section develops.
terra: The condemned ask to place their human and jinn misleaders underfoot among ٱلْأَسْفَلِينَ, exposing the end-value they now assign their former guides.
terra: Whatever people dispute has its حكم with God, and the speaker turns back to Him, joining decision and return.
terra: The two cultivators receive unlike returns: the Hereafter's harvest is increased, while the worldly cultivator gets some of it but no نَصِيبٍ in the Hereafter.

luna: Provision is sent down in measure for people; this is a specific economic counterpart to the source's claim that shares are allotted by measure. | terra: Unlimited worldly provision would provoke transgression, so God sends it by the measure He wills; measured livelihood is a boundary distinct from uncurtailed reward.
terra: Worldly possessions are temporary enjoyment, while what is with God is better and more enduring for believers.

luna: The source's dictionary sense of خَلَق as an apportioned share is made concrete by God distributing livelihoods among people in worldly life. | terra: God apportions livelihoods among people and raises some in degrees so they serve one another, a worldly instance of measured shares.
terra: Even imagined gold adornment is only worldly enjoyment, whereas the Hereafter with the Lord belongs to the God-fearing.

luna: Creation is followed by recompense for each soul's earnings without wrong; this joins the source's created human and just final valuation. | terra: Creation in truth has the purpose that every soul be recompensed for what it earned without injustice, linking خَلْق and measured return.
terra: Each community kneels and is summoned to its record, staging the judicial opening of communal ledgers.
terra: God's record speaks truth because deeds were copied, explaining the evidence behind the payment in 45:22.
terra: People receive ranks according to their works so that God may pay their deeds in full without wrong, uniting labor, valuation, and payment.
terra: Ruin is pronounced upon the disbelievers and their deeds are led astray, beginning a direct account of lost work.
terra: Because they hate what God sent down, He makes their works void, identifying why the labor in 47:8 loses value.
terra: Following what angers God and hating His pleasure results in works being nullified, another stated cause of failed assay.
terra: Those who disbelieve, bar the way, and oppose the messenger cannot harm God, but their own works are nullified.
terra: Believers are expressly warned not to nullify their works, presenting retained value as something obedience must guard.
terra: وَإِنَّ ٱلدِّينَ لَوَٰقِعٌ states that the promised recompense will certainly fall due.

luna: The source describes people challenged for denying repayment; these speakers ask mockingly when the “يوم الدين” will be, voicing the same resistance. | terra: The mockers ask when يَوْمُ ٱلدِّينِ will be, another stance of disbelief toward the due account.
luna: This repeats the liability image: each person is pledged for what they earned, a specific counterpart to the source's debt-and-account sense.
luna: God recompenses wrongdoers for their deeds and gives good-doers the best reward, a direct two-sided settlement like the source's account.

luna: The source's dictionary form عَمَلٌ links work to its wage; this says a person has only what they strive for, the work side of the account. | terra: A human has only what he strove for, establishing the work side of the section's wage equation.
luna: The preceding striving is to be seen here, so the work is presented for assessment before recompense. | terra: The striving named in 53:39 will be seen, so no work escapes appraisal.

luna: This completes the sequence with full recompense for the striving in 53:39; the source's labor-and-wage image is explicit. | terra: The seen striving is then repaid with the fullest repayment, completing work, assessment, and wage.

luna: This joins the source's creation root to measure directly: “خلقناه بقدر” says everything created is by measure. | terra: Everything is created بِقَدَرٍ, directly supporting the section's link between خَلْق and measure.
terra: Everything the wrongdoers did is in the records, so no work vanishes before assessment.
terra: Every small and great thing is inscribed, defining the ledger's precision.

luna: The source's balanced coin finds a cosmic counterpart in the “ميزان” placed with the raised heaven. | terra: God's setting of the ميزان alongside the raised heaven gives the commercial balance a created and moral order.

luna: This continues the balance image by forbidding transgression in the scale, the boundary that keeps measure just. | terra: This ayah forbids transgression in the balance set in 55:7, marking the boundary between sound assay and corrupted measure.

luna: The command to establish weight with justice and not reduce the balance makes the source's exact-weight coin an ethical measure too. | terra: أَقِيمُوا ٱلْوَزْنَ بِٱلْقِسْطِ joins the section's ق و م root to exact, just weighing and expressly forbids making the scale deficient.
terra: The punishment is identified as the guests' reception on يَوْمِ ٱلدِّينِ, the hostile payout for their course.

luna: The source cites “غير مدينين” as denial of being held to account; this challenge asks the deniers to return the soul if they are not indebted or answerable. | terra: The deathbed challenge calls its addressees غَيْرَ مَدِينِينَ, precisely the section's د ي ن sense of being liable for repayment or recompense.
terra: After 56:86 challenges those claiming they owe no recompense, this ayah demands that they return the departing soul if truthful; تَرْجِعُونَهَا makes ر د د the test of that claim.

luna: A goodly loan to God is multiplied and followed by a noble reward, a close Qur'anic instance of the source's debt-and-compensation sense. | terra: The one who lends God a good loan receives it multiplied and an honorable wage, placing loan and wage in one account.
terra: No ransom is accepted from hypocrites or disbelievers; the final liability cannot be discharged with a substitute payment.
terra: Charitable men and women who lend the good loan receive multiplication and a noble wage, specifying who is credited.
terra: Worldly life swells like admired growth then becomes debris, while the Hereafter holds punishment or forgiveness; the ayah exposes temporary apparent value.
terra: Book and ميزان are sent so people may uphold justice, making the scale an instrument of divine social judgment rather than a merely commercial tool.
luna: The division of captured property among specified recipients makes the source's allotted-share image concrete and states that it should not circulate only among the rich.
luna: The source's market vocabulary meets the explicit offer “تجارة تنجيكم”; this ayah frames belief and effort as a salvific transaction.
luna: This specifies what the trade in 61:10 asks for—faith and striving with wealth and selves—linking effort to its return.
luna: The trade described in 61:10–11 is settled here with forgiveness and the promised gardens; this ayah supplies the return on the transaction.
terra: People break away for trade and diversion, but what is with God is better than both and He is the best provider, a market choice corrected from the pulpit.

luna: He creates and shapes human beings, making their forms beautiful; this gives a direct creation-and-valuation counterpart to the source's best-form image. | terra: God forms humans and makes their forms good, and the ayah ends with the destination to Him, linking fine formation with eventual return.

luna: This repeats the lending image and promises multiplication and forgiveness, reinforcing the source's sense of payment returned. | terra: A good loan is multiplied and forgiven, so divine repayment includes both credited increase and canceled liability.

luna: God has set a measure for everything, echoing the source's claim that allotted shares are measured. | terra: God has made a measure for everything, setting a universal boundary beside the reward that is not curtailed.

luna: This independently repeats the wage for nursing work, a direct example of the source's work-for-payment relation. | terra: Mothers who nurse are to be given أُجُورَهُنَّ, a concrete labor payment whose fairness grounds the eschatological wage image.
luna: Human life and death are made a test of who is best in deed; this explains why the source's fitting and subsequent weighing lead to reward or loss.

luna: The source hears مَمْنُونٍ as an unshortened, measured wage; this promises the Prophet an “أجر غير ممنون,” repeating that wage formulation. | terra: The promise أَجْرًا غَيْرَ مَمْنُونٍ supplies another direct Quranic setting for a payment that is neither cut down nor exhausted.
terra: The successful person is handed his record in the right hand and invites others to read it, the visible presentation preceding his statement about حساب in 69:20.
terra: The joyful recipient of the record explains that he expected to meet his حساب, joining present valuation to prior accountability.
terra: The failed person receives the record in the left hand and wishes it had never been given, setting up his ignorance of the account in 69:26.
terra: The recipient of the other record laments that he did not know what his حساب would be, the stance that leaves the account disastrously unpaid.
terra: Those who affirm يَوْمِ ٱلدِّينِ embody the believing stance opposite the denial challenged in surah 95.
terra: Belief removes fear of both unfair loss and oppressive excess, setting boundaries on the account in both directions.

luna: The command to offer God a goodly loan is followed by finding good sent ahead and a greater reward, linking lending to later settlement. | terra: Good sent ahead is found with God as better and greater in wage, while the good loan figures as the advance entered in that account.
terra: The command not to give with a view to obtaining more uses the other م ن ن field to forbid treating generosity as an investment seeking enlarged return.
luna: The source frames final settlement through owing and repayment; this says every soul is held in pledge for what it earned.

luna: The speakers confess that they used to deny the Day of Recompense, a direct example of the denial challenged in the source's account of الدِّين. | terra: The condemned confess that they used to deny يَوْمِ ٱلدِّينِ, showing denial entered as a charge in the final reckoning.
terra: The human begins as a drop, then is created and proportioned; this repeats the sound formation that precedes the question of resurrection and recompense.
terra: After 75:38's created and proportioned human, this ayah asks whether that Maker can raise the dead, carrying formation into final accountability.
terra: The Garden is called a recompense and the recipients' striving is thanked, linking recognized labor to its payment.
terra: جَزَاءً وِفَاقًا describes a recompense fitted to the deed, the debit side of equivalent settlement.
terra: The Lord's جَزَاءً عَطَاءً حِسَابًا presents the reward as an ample, reckoned gift, balancing measure and generosity.

luna: The source links خ ل ق to measured allotment; this says God creates the human from a drop and determines him, joining human formation to measure. | terra: God creates the human from a drop and measures or proportions him, a direct creation-side counterpart to the section's assayed human being.

luna: The source's “best calibration” for the human has a close counterpart in being created, proportioned, and balanced: “فعدلك.” | terra: خَلَقَكَ فَسَوَّىٰكَ فَعَدَلَكَ depicts the human as created, proportioned, and balanced before the surah confronts denial of recompense.

luna: This continues the formation in 82:7 by saying God composed the person in whatever form He willed, clarifying the source's image of fitted creation. | terra: This ayah completes 82:7 by saying God assembled the human in whatever form He willed, specifying the Maker behind the body's sound proportion.
terra: كَلَّا بَلْ تُكَذِّبُونَ بِٱلدِّينِ is the closest direct echo of surah 95's question about denying دِين after being created and balanced.
terra: The wicked enter the Fire on يَوْمِ ٱلدِّينِ, giving the term's recompense sense a concrete outcome.

luna: This names the Day of Recompense and asks what will make it understood, sharing the source's focus on the reality of the final account. | terra: The repeated question وَمَا أَدْرَىٰكَ مَا يَوْمُ ٱلدِّينِ magnifies the day on which the section's debt is settled.

luna: The next ayah repeats the question about the Day of Recompense; its repetition stresses the day whose settlement the source describes. | terra: The second formulation repeats and intensifies the demand to reckon with يَوْمُ ٱلدِّينِ rather than dismiss it.

luna: This answers the preceding repeated question by describing a day when no soul can help another and command belongs to God, completing the account's finality. | terra: On that day no soul controls anything for another and the command belongs to God, defining the final Judge's exclusive authority.

luna: The source's correctly weighted coin has a sharp opposite in the “مطففين,” who cheat in measures; this ayah names the fraud. | terra: The warning to المطففين names the moral opposite of the section's full-weight coin.

luna: The preceding warning is made concrete: these people take their full measure from others, the opposite of fair calibration. | terra: The defrauders demand full measure when they receive, exposing a self-serving standard of value.

luna: They short others when measuring or weighing; this is the exact dishonest reversal of the source's full-weight standard. | terra: They diminish what they measure or weigh out to others, the direct reversal of a full-weight payment.

luna: After the warning about cheating measures in 83:1–3, this asks whether the cheaters expect to be raised, tying the dishonest balance to reckoning. | terra: The question whether such traders expect resurrection carries the market scene into the final reckoning.

luna: This specifies the resurrection in 83:4 as a great day, giving the weighing fraud a judgment horizon. | terra: This ayah identifies the resurrection anticipated in 83:4 as a tremendous day, when crooked measures are answered for.

luna: The great day is the day people stand before the Lord of the worlds; it completes the link between 83's false measures and the source's final accounting. | terra: People stand before the Lord of the worlds, joining the market ledger to the wider ق و م field of standing for judgment.
luna: After 83:1–6 links cheating weights with resurrection, this names the record of the wicked, extending the measuring scene into a recorded verdict.
luna: This calls the wicked person's record a written register, specifying how the verdict introduced in 83:7 is kept.

luna: In the same surah that condemns short measure, this names those who deny “بيوم الدين,” joining false weighing to the source's repayment day. | terra: The transgressing deniers are those who deny يَوْمِ ٱلدِّينِ, carrying the crooked-scale passage into explicit denial of settlement.
luna: The corresponding record for the righteous is in Illiyyun, giving the source's separate bad valuation a positive counterpart.
luna: This also identifies the righteous record as written, completing the parallel with the wicked register in 83:9.
terra: Receiving the record in the right hand supplies the documentary scene that makes the easy account of 84:8 intelligible.
terra: The recipient of the book in the right hand receives an easy حساب, making the manner of final settlement explicit.
terra: Receiving the record from behind the back marks the rejected side of the ledger before the call for destruction.

luna: This ayah also promises “أجر غير ممنون” for believers who do good; it is a close repeated formulation of the source's wage image. | terra: This ayah repeats the section's exact pairing of faith, righteous works, and أَجْرٌ غَيْرُ مَمْنُونٍ outside surah 95.

luna: God creates and proportionally forms here, a close parallel to the source's human made in “أحسن تقويم.” | terra: God creates and proportions, a concise parallel to the human being made fit before valuation.

luna: Creation is followed by determining and guiding; this makes the measured order behind the source's creation image explicit. | terra: God determines and guides, extending proportion into an assigned course and end.
terra: The addressees prefer the nearer life, identifying the mistaken valuation that the section's assay exposes.
terra: The Hereafter is better and more lasting, supplying the corrected value judgment after 87:16.

luna: The source cites this return to God; the next ayah supplies the account, so this verse contributes the return that begins the settlement. | terra: The section cites this ayah as the first half of its closing ledger: the assessed human being's return is to God.

luna: This says the account is God's after the return in 88:25, completing the source's pairing of return and reckoning. | terra: Following 88:25's return, this ayah assigns their حساب to God, completing the section's movement from appraisal to final settlement.
terra: A human reads generous provision as God's declaration that he is honored, exposing a faulty human method of appraisal.
terra: When provision is measured tightly, the same human concludes he is humiliated; the pair shows that market quantity is not God's final valuation.

luna: The source's weighing image applies even at the smallest scale: a deed of “مثقال ذرة” of good is seen and therefore cannot be lost from the account. | terra: Even an atom's weight of good is seen, a minute assay below which no earned value disappears.

luna: The corresponding particle-weight of evil is also seen; this is the adverse side of the source's account, where nothing escapes assessment. | terra: Even an atom's weight of evil is seen, making the same scale exact on the debit side.
luna: The source's coin weighed at full measure parallels the heavy scales that open the surah's final weighing scene. | terra: The one whose مَوَازِينُ are heavy passes the judgment's assay.

luna: This ayah gives the favorable consequence of the heavy measure in 101:6, completing the source's image of sound value receiving its due. | terra: A pleasing life is the outcome assigned to the heavy scales of 101:6, showing what that weight is worth.

luna: Light scales reverse the source's sound, fully calibrated coin and introduce the failing measure. | terra: Light مَوَازِينُ make the principal reversal vivid: apparent human holdings carry insufficient weight.

luna: The preceding ayah's light scales lead here to “هاوية”; this completes the contrast between the source's proper measure and a debased outcome. | terra: The light scales lead downward to an abyss, turning loss of weight into the lowest destination.
luna: After 101:9 ends with the light-scaled person's destination, this identifies al-Hawiyah as a blazing fire and completes that outcome.
terra: The person who gathers and repeatedly counts wealth treats enumeration as security and value.
terra: He imagines his wealth makes him permanent, confusing counted property with enduring worth.
terra: The hoarder is instead cast into the Crusher, the final rejection of his self-assessed value.
terra: أَرَءَيْتَ ٱلَّذِى يُكَذِّبُ بِٱلدِّينِ echoes surah 95's challenge, then tests that denial by its treatment of vulnerable people.
